note: A named matrix, not a product search. Every row changes one understandable part of the arena and all rows in a block use the same deterministic seed interval, so a difference is attributable to geometry or toughness rather than to sampling noise. Blocks A-Q used seeds 1..1000; block K/R/S used 100001..103000 (an independent interval, to check that the finalist was not fitted to the tuning seeds). The brief's search regions are pass rates of 90-96 / 65-80 / 35-50 / 15-28 / 3-8 percent and a race-success rate of 20-40 percent.

blocks.question: does the shrunken arena (inner 6.5, spacing 3.0, ball 0.53) work at all, and where does the ladder sit?
blocks.read: B is the shape; the 2-slot shell 3 is what lifts shell 3 from 14.8 to 30.9 percent. Slowing the ball buys a calmer bed and costs escape rate one-for-one, so speed stays at 10 and density is managed in audio instead.

blocks.question: can population be raised without leaving the pass-rate regions?
blocks.read: No. G is the first row with all four outer shells inside the regions and its population is 12. H is the answer to 'make shell 1 harder': 18 panels barely moves its pass rate (96.8 percent) and costs the hook - median first clone 0.84 s to 1.45 s, 75th percentile past 2.7 s. Population and the difficulty regions are in genuine conflict; see the phase document.

blocks.question: where exactly inside the regions should the ladder sit?
blocks.read: K is the ladder. Q buys one ball of population for 3.6 more collisions a second, which is the wrong trade at this density.

blocks.question: does the finalist hold on seeds it was not tuned on, and is the final wall the right hardness?

rows.label: R_s4_soft
rows.read: lowering the outermost threshold from 16 to 14 moves nothing: the final wall is almost never crossed by breaking it, so its toughness is not what gates the race

rows.label: S_s4_wider
rows.read: SELECTED. Widening the outermost opening from 1/72 to 1/66 of the shell is what moves the race-success rate, because the moving opening is the route almost every winner takes
